$comment: Single source of truth for what Soraya sells. Every skill and the landing page read this file. Change a drawer here, not in five places.

mesghal.note: Iranian mesghal-e sharie. Saffron in Iran is traded in mesghal, not grams. Always store saffron quantities in mesghal and derive grams; never round-trip through grams.

saffron-negin.notes: Long unbroken threads including the upper stigma. Highest visual grade of the three red trims; this is the drawer the customer opens first.

saffron-powder.notes: Used only inside tea bags. Deliberately the same lot as saffron-negin, ground — the box carries one saffron grade in inventory, not two.

kakuti-powder.notes: Persian mountain mint. Aromatic between mint and thyme; traditionally digestive and carminative.

kakuti-leaf.notes: Costed at 0.9x the per-gram price of kakuti-powder. This is a deliberate simplification agreed by the owner, not a measured figure — see pricing skill.

rose-buds.notes: Whole closed buds. The visual hero of the rose drawer — buds photograph far better than petals.

rose-petals.notes: Loose dried petals, for infusion and garnish.

soraya-teabag.hsCodeNote: Blended herbal infusion containing no Camellia sinensis may classify under 1211.90 instead. Confirm with the Omani customs broker before the first shipment — the two headings carry different duty treatment.
soraya-teabag.notes: Per-bag fill weights are NOT yet decided. Typical infusion bag is 1.5-2.5 g total. Owner to set the ratio; until then treat qty as unknown rather than guessing.

drawer-cube.form: Rigid cube that opens to reveal stacked sliding drawers, in the manner of a Japanese jubako / sushi presentation box.
drawer-cube.notes: Most expensive and most presentable format. Dimensions unset — they follow from the six fill volumes, so decide contents first, box second. See packaging skill.

slim-sleeve.form: Single-drawer rigid sleeve, same materials and print as the cube.

carton.form: Folding carton, litho-printed, no rigid board.

soraya.nameNote: The flagship carries the house name. Every other SKU is named after something it is about, never after what it lacks.
soraya.notes: kakuti-leaf quantity is a range in the owner's brief. A range cannot be costed or label-declared — resolve to a single count (or a declared net weight) before quoting.

sofreh.nameNote: The spread laid for guests. Renamed from the brief's 'Lady with Taste' — the range names one evocative word each, and 'sufra' reads natively in Arabic.
sofreh.notes: All three crops without the drawer cube and without the tea bags. Sits directly under the flagship, so its size and price must be set together with Soraya's or it cannibalises rather than laddering.

iran.notes: Saffron and nothing else — for the buyer who wants the spice, not the story. Also the price anchor. Natural sizes are 1 and 2 mesghal; anchor against Soraya so the flagship still reads as the better value per mesghal.

peace.notes: Lowest barrier to a first order and the only SKU cheap enough to give away as a sample. Counts of 12 or 20 are conventional.
